sources.title: New Tools for Peak Memory Scheduling
sources.read_scope: primary abstract and submission history; v1 Dec21 2023
sources.findings: Weighted one-shot black pebbling; dominant schedules and series-parallel FPT by outdegree. Strong NP-completeness even for out-trees/pumpkins.
sources.inference_for_27: Do not infer arbitrary-DAG feasibility or a polynomial exact solver from tree structure. A dominant subgraph schedule needs compatibility with original external direct consumers, workspace, sinks and deadlines. Prior final-live filter negatives remain frozen.

sources.title: Graph Transformations for Memory Peak Minimization by Scheduling
sources.read_scope: author abstract and Jan2025 corrected-version listing; no fullpaper algorithm read
sources.findings: Peak-preserving task graph reductions; SP-DAG composition and branch-and-bound on reduced graphs.
sources.inference_for_27: Investigate compositional scheduling only after checking exact shared-output lifetime and workspace semantics; do not merge original vertices, drop outside consumers or claim its reductions preserve contest AIC/AIV/time constraints without proof.

sources.title: Parallel Scheduling of Task Graphs with Minimal Memory Requirements
sources.findings: Find a sequential memory-minimal schedule for supported graph classes, then memory-aware parallel list scheduling. Its stated memory guarantee is conditional on its model and sequential-peak constraint.
sources.inference_for_27: Separate finding an original-DAG feasible sequential order from parallel/time scheduling diagnostics. Does not prove our heterogeneous AIC/AIV/deadline model. First collect actual candidate failure stages rather than infer them from total work.

sources.title: FusionRCG: Orchestrating Recursive Computation Graphs across GPU Memory Hierarchies
sources.read_scope: primary abstract and v1 May11/v2 May13 submission history
sources.findings: Liveness-aware ordering, algebraic dimensionality reduction and GPU hierarchy mapping in electron-repulsion integral recurrences.
sources.inference_for_18_27: Only liveness-aware ordering is a plausible conceptual transfer. Algebraic fusion changes identities and GPU hierarchy choices change the problem; neither is authorized by the strict original-operation/window or graph resource requirements. Reported A100 benefits do not support local contest speed claims.
